text: Paul Taylor's biocentric ethics grounds the inherent worth of an organism in which of the following?
choices: Its capacity to feel pain and pleasure
Its role in maintaining ecosystem stability
Its being a teleological center of life with a good of its own
Its possession of a nervous system
explanation: For Taylor, every living thing is a 'teleological center of life' with a good of its own, and that alone confers inherent worth, without requiring sentience. Grounding worth in the capacity to feel pain is the rival sentience-based view; grounding it in ecosystem stability is Leopold's land ethics; a nervous system is not a biocentric criterion at all.
